problems: The quote and number are verbatim (R029 p.26893: "The D10, D50, and D90 values were 7.5 μm, 44.1 μm, and 169.1 μm, respectively"). They were measured on a sieve fraction, though, not on KLS-1 as produced.

R029 §2.1 says: "In the present study, the lunar regolith simulant was passed through a no. 20 sieve (<850 μm) before use." As produced, KLS-1 is <4.75 mm: R081 says "only particles finer than 4.75 mm were used". The IJMST 2024 review (files/1643) also lists this material as "KLS-1 d <850". Under the exact-product and sieve-fraction rule, this does not support a D50 for KLS-1 itself.

If the curator accepts it, it needs a qualifier: '<850 μm fraction, laser diffraction'. R081 gives <0.075 mm = 48.92% by sieving, which implies a sieve-based D50 of roughly 75 μm for the full product (not derived here as a value).
'Publication Date: 2018-01-01' is the UNSW repository metadata for the article, not a statement about when KLS-1 was released. The article itself says it was "published online on October 25, 2017".

Group documents give a different development year. R111/ISECG p.61: "KICT already developed KLS-1 in 2015". Kang 2024 (the S031 NEW2) Table 1 row: "KLS-1 | 한국 | 2015년 | 바다". R081 also cites a 'KLS-1 production system (Baek et al. 2015)'.

Only a secondary review (IGG-01, files/1757) lists 'KLS-1 Korea 2018', citing Ryu 2018. The stored 2018 is at best the publication year of the characterisation paper. The curator should choose between 2015 (development) and 2018 (publication).
